prompt.en: A coax run is doubled in length using the same cable at the same frequency. What happens to loss stated in dB?

text.en: It becomes zero if the SWR is low.

explanation.en: For the same cable and frequency, dB loss accumulates with length.

prompt.en: What is a tuner at the radio mainly doing when it lets a solid-state transmitter run at rated power?

text.en: Transforming impedance so the transmitter sees a suitable load
Removing all loss from the feedline between tuner and antenna
Changing the antenna's physical length and radiation pattern
Replacing the need to find intermittent connectors

explanation.en: A tuner is an impedance-matching network; it does not change the actual radiation pattern or remove all feedline loss.

prompt.en: Why can a lossy feedline make an SWR reading at the desk look better than the antenna feed point really is?

text.en: The reflected wave is attenuated on its trip back to the meter.
The antenna stops radiating when the line is lossy.
The feedline changes every antenna into a dummy load.
The SWR meter reads polarization instead of voltage waves.

explanation.en: Loss reduces both forward and reflected energy; the return trip especially can hide the size of the mismatch from a station-end meter.
